children: Crude oil futures closed mixed on Thursday, with Brent ticking lower while WTI jumped on bullish inventory data and reports that the Trump administration is considering easing some sanctions on the world's "shadow fleet" of tankers to try to increase tanker supply and lower the cost of moving crude.

U.S. crude inventories fell by 8.6M barrels last week, the biggest drop since February and compared to expectations of a small stock build, in part due to shut-ins from Hurricane Isaias and strong refinery runs, the Energy Information Administration

U.S. commercial crude oil stocks excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve declined to 415.6M barrels in the week ended October 9 and were 3% below the five-year average for the time of year, the EIA said.

Domestic gasoline inventories rose by 3.5M barrels to 208.3M barrels and were 4% below the five-year average, and distillate fuel stocks fell by 2.5M barrels to 102.6M barrels and were 12% below the five-year average.

"Consumers might get some relief at the pump with gasoline prices, but the tight diesel situation keeps pressure on costs and inflation in the broader economy," David Russell of TradeStation said in a note.

Meanwhile, most analysts said a move to ease sanctions on tankers that form part of shadow fleets likely would have limited impact on boosting tanker availability, as shadow fleet ships still face sanctions ‌from other countries and lack the certification, insurance, and maintenance needed to enter mainstream trade.

The measure would have "virtually no impact on the current tanker crisis," analysts at ship-tracking firm Kpler said. "The proposal assumes that removing sanctions will ​translate into additional commercially available capacity. In practice, the relationship is far more complicated."
Aging ⁠vessels, uncertain seaworthiness and unresolved insurance, crewing and management arrangements would limit the ships' commercial appeal, the firm said.

Only ~24 ships out of 160 supertankers currently under U.S. ​sanctions could rejoin global trade ​once age is taken into account and tankers owned by Iran's National Tanker Company are excluded, according to Kpler.

Also, the International Energy Agency said emergency oil stock releases by member countries would exceed the 400M barrels agreed in March; 330M barrels have been released so far, with members pledging to expedite the remaining 100M barrels, including more than 20M barrels of diesel, the IEA said.
The Singapore-flagged
GFS Pride

sank while being towed to shore after it was struck near the Strait of Hormuz by a projectile from Iran, U.S. Central Command said, yet more than 40 vessels moved through the strait over the past 24 hours, suggesting flows are continuing.
Front-month Nymex crude
for November delivery rose for the sixth consecutive session, jumping 3% to $97.97/bbl, its highest close since September 18, while front-month Brent crude
for December delivery fell 0.1% to $105.92/bbl.
Front-month Nymex RBOB gasoline (
) for November delivery fell 2.4% to $3.1802/gal, and front-month Nymex November ULSD (
) slipped 1.6% to $4.8456/gal, the fourth decline in the past five sessions for both benchmarks.
Front Month Nymex natural gas
for November delivery rose 1.29% to $3.236/MMBtu, as the EIA reported a smaller-than-expected 67 Bcf storage injection for last week.

title: U.S. crude oil jumps on big inventory draw, potential shadow fleet sanctions relief
